method: COMPILED FROM 3 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.) 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)' (2025 (first edition 2011)), 21 claims; LICENCE: © Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Wounds Australia and the Wound Healing Society of Singapore. All rights reserved (read at the copyright page of the PDF). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI); Attaran RR, Edwards JM, Arena FJ, et al., Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions 4(8) '2025 SCAI Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Chronic Venous Disease' (published 30 June 2025), 6 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12462076). S3: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from International Union of Phlebology (UIP); Tan MKH, Lurie F, Bauza Moreno H, et al., Phlebology 39(7) 'Management of venous leg ulcers (International Union of Phlebology one-page guideline)' (published online 29 March 2024), 5 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11380361). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every edition 1.0 claim and anchor (S1, the 2025 Australian/NZ assessment section) unchanged and adds treatment: S2, the SCAI 2025 GRADE guideline on chronic venous disease (compression, ablation, sclerotherapy, perforator and iliocaval treatment), and S3, the UIP 2024 one-page VLU guideline (wound care, duplex, follow-up of non-healing ulcers). The Wounds Australia 2025 management section is still unpublished; the ESVS 2022 chronic venous disease guideline (CC BY) was behind a bot challenge and was not read.

claims.claim: **Venous ulcers are among the commonest lower leg ulcers:** about half of all hard-to-heal wounds and around 42% of leg ulcers seen in a typical Australian wound service. They affect all ages but more often older people.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **They arise from sustained venous hypertension,** caused by venous obstruction (such as thrombosis), valve incompetence with reflux, or both. Post-thrombotic syndrome develops after up to 50% of DVTs.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors include genetics, prior varicose vein surgery, venous disease, phlebitis, DVT, heart failure, obesity, immobility and past leg trauma;** a weak calf pump, poor mobility and reduced ankle movement speed progression. Untreated venous disease worsens, so ulcers often recur.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess every person with a lower leg ulcer comprehensively at the start and repeatedly after,** to establish the cause, shape the plan and referrals, and track outcomes.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Establish the ulcer's cause before starting compression.** Compression can injure a critically ischaemic limb, and it can worsen ulcers of other causes such as pyoderma gangrenosum.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every patient with a lower leg ulcer needs an initial vascular assessment** (vascular history and examination of the lower leg).
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Screen for peripheral arterial disease when there are risk factors, a non-healing ulcer or a suggestive history or wound:** at minimum, palpate pulses and do an ABI, TBI or absolute systolic toe pressure (unless contraindicated). Transcutaneous oxygen or Doppler waveforms can be added as indicated.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also examine the skin, sensation, oedema and mobility, and describe venous signs with the CEAP classification;** severity scales can track them over time.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess leg pain, and wound pain when an ulcer is open, with a validated tool;** assess quality of life with a validated tool, and screen nutrition and hydration.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess the wound fully at baseline and again at every dressing procedure:** history, healing phase, size, bed, edge, surrounding skin, exudate and signs of infection.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ABI (handheld Doppler) is the usual point-of-care arterial screen;** TBI may be more accurate and is needed when vessels are calcified. The aims are to diagnose and follow PAD and to keep compression away from limbs with inadequate arterial supply.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Compression is not simply banned by any sign of PAD:** the ESVS guideline contraindicates sustained compression only below ABI 0.6, ankle pressure 60 mmHg or toe pressure 30 mmHg (PAD itself being ABI below 0.8). Guidelines allow cautious compression at ABI 0.5 to 0.8 when there are no arterial signs or symptoms.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **TBI is more sensitive than ABI, especially with diabetes or kidney disease;** a TBI above 0.7 is normal and a reasonable threshold for applying compression.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspect calcified, incompressible arteries with weak or absent pulses or an ABI above 1.4 (above 1.3 with diabetes or chronic kidney disease):** do a TBI or toe pressure, or refer. Never diagnose PAD from one test alone, and repeat the vascular assessment regularly, with new symptoms or when healing stalls.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Duplex ultrasound is the investigation of choice** for vascular cause, site and extent, but needs specialist skills and is unavailable in most wound care settings.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer to a vascular expert:** anyone with venous symptoms or an active ulcer never reviewed by one; anyone whose screening shows significant PAD; and anyone in a setting where PAD screening cannot be done.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Refer for vascular investigation at ABI below 0.6, TBI below 0.5 or toe pressure below 70 mmHg;** consider it at ABI below 0.9, TBI below 0.6, toe pressure below 95 mmHg or biphasic/monophasic Doppler waveforms.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urgent:** a traumatic leg injury in someone with chronic venous insufficiency (DVT risk) goes to a vascular expert or wound clinic promptly. Also investigate thigh-level oedema and unequal arm systolic pressures.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Don't hold up initial care while waiting for multidisciplinary input;** refer anyone at nutritional risk to a dietitian.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Re-examine the diagnosis if an ulcer has not healed by 25–40% within 2–4 weeks of best-practice care;** less than 25% healing at two weeks is an early warning of delay.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Perfusion adequate for healing (consensus):** a palpable dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial pulse, ABI above 0.6 and below 1.4, toe pressure 30 to 35 mmHg and an audible triphasic or biphasic Doppler signal. These markers need more validation.
claims.locator: Venous Leg Ulcer Guideline Committee (Wounds Australia, New Zealand Wound Care Society, Hong Kong Enterostomal Therapists Association, Wound Healing Society of Singapore); E. Haesler (Ed.), 'Clinical Practice Guideline for Venous Leg Ulcers: Assessment (2nd edition)', 2025 (first edition 2011), https://woundsaustralia.org/int/woundsaus/uploads/Publications/venous%20leg%20ulcer%20assessment%20section-2025.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With appropriate treatment most venous ulcers heal within 6 months, but up to 70% recur within 5 years.** See the patient regularly to track healing; if it is acceptable, carry on.
claims.locator: International Union of Phlebology (UIP); Tan MKH, Lurie F, Bauza Moreno H, et al., Phlebology 39(7), 'Management of venous leg ulcers (International Union of Phlebology one-page guideline)', published online 29 March 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11380361/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every venous ulcer needs compression** (SCAI: strong recommendation, moderate certainty); stronger compression grades may work better. Compared with none, compression raised healing at 12 months (risk ratio 1.77; about 311 more healed per 1000) and shortened time to healing (hazard ratio 2.17).
claims.locator: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI); Attaran RR, Edwards JM, Arena FJ, et al., Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions 4(8), '2025 SCAI Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Chronic Venous Disease', published 30 June 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12462076/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Compression can be given by bandages, stockings, Velcro wraps or pneumatic pumps, alone or combined.** Conservative care also includes venotonic drugs, lifestyle change, weight loss when relevant and wound care; poor adherence is its main weakness.
claims.locator: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI); Attaran RR, Edwards JM, Arena FJ, et al., Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions 4(8), '2025 SCAI Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Chronic Venous Disease', published 30 June 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12462076/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Wound care (UIP):** good wound care, infection control and compression for every patient. Measure and photograph the ulcer; take a swab for culture only when pain, discharge, spreading redness or fever suggest infection.
claims.locator: International Union of Phlebology (UIP); Tan MKH, Lurie F, Bauza Moreno H, et al., Phlebology 39(7), 'Management of venous leg ulcers (International Union of Phlebology one-page guideline)', published online 29 March 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11380361/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pentoxifylline** is described as a useful add-on for healing; among skin grafts, only bilayer artificial skin had evidence of better healing in a Cochrane review.
claims.locator: International Union of Phlebology (UIP); Tan MKH, Lurie F, Bauza Moreno H, et al., Phlebology 39(7), 'Management of venous leg ulcers (International Union of Phlebology one-page guideline)', published online 29 March 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11380361/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Duplex ultrasound is the gold-standard test for reflux and obstruction,** including the iliac veins. Truncal reflux (great, small or anterior accessory saphenous vein) should be removed with endovenous ablation such as radiofrequency or laser, and reflux at the ulcer site treated locally.
claims.locator: International Union of Phlebology (UIP); Tan MKH, Lurie F, Bauza Moreno H, et al., Phlebology 39(7), 'Management of venous leg ulcers (International Union of Phlebology one-page guideline)', published online 29 March 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11380361/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Great (with or without small) saphenous reflux: ablation plus compression rather than compression alone** (SCAI: conditional, low certainty). People with ulcers gain most and should be offered ablation early: it shortened healing by a mean of 31.73 days and cut recurrence at 2 years (risk ratio 0.39).
claims.locator: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI); Attaran RR, Edwards JM, Arena FJ, et al., Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions 4(8), '2025 SCAI Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Chronic Venous Disease', published 30 June 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12462076/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ulcer without truncal reflux: foam sclerotherapy plus conservative care** (conditional, low certainty), aimed at varicosities under the ulcer bed. **Perforator reflux feeding an ulcer: perforator ablation plus conservative care** (conditional, low certainty). SCAI makes no recommendation on phlebectomy for ulcers.
claims.locator: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI); Attaran RR, Edwards JM, Arena FJ, et al., Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions 4(8), '2025 SCAI Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Chronic Venous Disease', published 30 June 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12462076/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Symptomatic deep (iliocaval) obstruction: venoplasty or stenting plus conservative care** (conditional, low certainty), usually for at least 50% lumen narrowing on intravascular ultrasound with severe symptoms. In the one trial, of 207 patients who had failed conservative care, ulcer healing was 90% with stenting against 40% without. No recommendation is made for femoral vein stenting.
claims.locator: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI); Attaran RR, Edwards JM, Arena FJ, et al., Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions 4(8), '2025 SCAI Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Chronic Venous Disease', published 30 June 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12462076/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A non-healing ulcer with suspected mixed arterial disease may benefit from arterial revascularisation;** saphenous ablation may also use up a vein needed later for bypass, which matters with advanced coronary or peripheral arterial disease.
claims.locator: Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions (SCAI); Attaran RR, Edwards JM, Arena FJ, et al., Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions 4(8), '2025 SCAI Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Chronic Venous Disease', published 30 June 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12462076/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If the ulcer is not improving or is getting worse, investigate further:** consider a biopsy to rule out malignancy and blood tests for thrombophilia and connective tissue disease, and consider skin grafts or skin substitutes. Refer urgently to a vascular specialist.
claims.locator: International Union of Phlebology (UIP); Tan MKH, Lurie F, Bauza Moreno H, et al., Phlebology 39(7), 'Management of venous leg ulcers (International Union of Phlebology one-page guideline)', published online 29 March 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11380361/, retrieved 2026-09-24
